newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bonds weaken on pre-auction attack.
newsitem.headline: Russian bonds weaken on pre-auction attack.

text.p: Russian government securities prices fell on Monday on speculative selling of OFZ interest-bearing bonds ahead of Wednesday's auctions, dealers said.
But dealers said they expected the central bank to support bonds on Tuesday to head off further speculative attacks.
The rouble firmed initially but fell back on typical pre-auction selling as foreigners raised rouble funds.
* Average yield rose to 18.6 pct from 18.1 pct on Friday
* Turnover 2.27 trillion roubules vs 2.22 trillion
* Dealers transferred 1.60 trillion roubles to accounts before trading
* Central bank did not buy or sell on behalf of finance ministry

As in recent weeks, the central bank will repay a tax-exempt OFZ bond early on a voluntary basis after Wednesday's auction.
It will then offer recent issues of taxable OFZ bonds from the finance ministry's portfolio, mainly to allow those who took up the repayment offer to replenish their holdings.
At such sessions previous OFZ issues are sold at their average price on the preceding Tuesday, giving some operators reason to push prices down in the run-up to the auction.
The two most recent issues, series 24014 and series 24015, fell on Monday to 97.92 and 96.93 respectively from 98.40 and 97.12 on Friday.
"It is unlikely that the central bank does not understand what this speculation is all about, and I think we will see its support for OFZ bonds tomorrow," said one dealer.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
